title: Computers

menu.makeCurrent.note: Programs, Files and the Agent then work on this computer
current.ask.title: Make {{name}} the current computer?
current.ask.body: The top bar then shows {{name}}. Pages that work on one computer at a time work on it. Nothing on {{name}} changes. This browser keeps the choice.

confirm.restart.title: Restart {{name}}?

confirm.resume.title: Resume {{name}}?

bulk.body: This applies to every selected computer. Open sessions on them end.
op.pending: The request may have gone through. Check the current state before trying again.

op.pendingElsewhere: A change sent from the Programs page may have gone through. Check it there.

default.help: Commands and tools that do not name a computer use this one.

access.set.both.body: {{name}} has access rules of its own, and its project's rules apply too.
access.open.body: Anyone with the address of {{name}} can open its programs.
access.unknown.body: We could not tell who can reach {{name}}.
access.unchecked.body: We couldn't check who can reach {{name}} just now. Try again in a moment.

realm.noneBody: {{name}} is in no realm, so it is listed only when All realms is chosen. A key limited to a realm can't see or manage it.
empty.title: No computers match
empty.body: Change the filters or get a new computer.
detail.gone: This computer is no longer here
detail.goneBody: It may have been deleted or moved out of this view.
colour.tip: This computer's colour. It marks the computer in tabs, lists and Boards. Click to change.
colour.title: Colour of {{name}}
colour.label: Colour
desktop.noAddress: No address for this desktop here
desktop.noAddress.body: This computer's server, or the address the Hub uses for computers, is not known yet, so its desktop cannot be shown or opened.
desktop.slow.body: It may still be starting, or this browser cannot show it inside the Hub. Open it in a new tab to see what it says.
desktop.keys: While the desktop has focus, your keys go to it. Press Leave desktop to use the Hub's shortcuts again.
desktop.listDown: Couldn't read which desktops this computer has, so only the ones this tab knows are listed.
desktop.env.listDown: Couldn't read which desktop environments this computer has, so the usual ones are listed.
desktop.stop.title: Stop desktop {{n}}?
desktop.stop.body: Every app open on it closes and unsaved work is lost. Stopping it frees the memory it uses.
desktop.switch.title: Switch desktop {{n}} to {{env}}?
desktop.switch.body: The desktop restarts with {{env}}: every app open on it closes and unsaved work is lost.
desktop.off.body: Its display and apps were closed, which frees the memory they used. Start it to open it again.
desktop.busy.body: A screenshot of it was still being taken, so nothing was stopped. Try again in a moment.
desktop.failed.body: Nothing was stopped. Try again, or show the desktop again.
desktop.unknown: Desktop {{n}} may not have stopped yet
desktop.unknown.body: The answer was lost, so it may have stopped. Stopping again is safe: a desktop that already stopped just says so.
desktop.unknown.onWay: A Stop is still on its way, maybe from another tab. This changes when it answers.
desktop.unknown.check: A Stop sent for it answered somewhere else, or its answer was lost. Check again to read whether it is still open.
desktop.reset: Desktop {{n}} stopped, but it was not reset
desktop.reset.unknown: Desktop {{n}} stopped, but we couldn't tell whether it was reset
desktop.reset.body: Starting it now may wait for a display that does not come. Stop again to finish: the part already done is skipped.
desktop.replaced: Desktop {{n}}'s session changed while it was stopping
desktop.replaced.body: It may have been opened again, so it was left as it is. Show it, or stop it.
desktop.listed.body: Its session is still listed, so it may be running with apps open. Show it, or stop it.
desktop.reopened.body: It was started again after you stopped it here, maybe from another tab or after the computer restarted. Show it, or stop it.
fact.imageTip: The image name as Hoody stores it: {{raw}}
fact.imageUnknown: This computer's image is not known.

facts.title: Details
use.terminal.name: Terminal
use.screen.name: Desktop

use.files.name: Files
use.browser.name: Browser
use.browser.body: A web browser that runs on the computer.

usage.title: Usage
usage.off: Off. Turn it on to read CPU, memory and disk.
usage.shared: CPU and memory are shared with the other computers on {{server}}; none is reserved for this one. Disk space comes from the same server, and a computer can have its own disk limit.
usage.sharedNoServer: CPU and memory are shared with the other computers on this computer's server; none is reserved for this one. Disk space comes from the same server, and a computer can have its own disk limit.
connect.linksLede: Each program has its own address. Copy it or open it.
connect.linksStopped: {{name}} is stopped. Start it to open its programs.
connect.apiLede: These programs have no page to open: your scripts and apps call their addresses. Copy an address or show it as a QR code.
connect.qrWarn: Anyone with this address can use the program. Do not share it.
ssh.title: SSH access
ssh.lede: Connect to {{name}} from your own terminal with your SSH key. The terminal in your browser needs no key: it is under Program links.
ssh.cli.title: With the command line
ssh.cli.body: Install the Hoody command line and sign in. Then use it with {{name}}.
ssh.cli.where: In a terminal on your device
ssh.cli.sdk: Libraries for your own code: sdk.hoody.com
ssh.gateway.title: Through hoody.com
ssh.gateway.body: ssh hoody.com opens a hosted session with the Hoody CLI from an interactive SSH client; nothing is installed on your device.
ssh.error.private: That looks like a private key. Never paste a private key. Paste the public one.
ssh.error.notkey: That does not look like a public SSH key.
sshd.title: SSH key for {{name}}
sshd.lede: The public key lets you connect to this computer from your own SSH client; the terminal in your browser needs no key. Each computer needs its own key: a key can be on one computer only.
create.sshNotInstalled: The new computer was created without its SSH key.
create.sshNotInstalledBody: That key is already on another computer. Add a different key under SSH access.
sshd.inUse: This key is already on another computer. Make a new key for this computer and paste that one.
sshd.fieldHelp: Starts with ssh-ed25519 or ssh-rsa. Never paste a private key.
sshd.removeBody: Remove the SSH key from {{name}}? You will not be able to connect over SSH until you add one.
run.label: Command
run.notSent: The command wasn't sent. Nothing ran.
run.noOutputCame: No output came back. The command may still have run.
run.unknownShort: The command may have gone through
run.hint: Runs once on the computer. Press Enter to run.
run.historyEmptyWhy: Commands you run on this computer are kept here
run.historyClear.title: Clear the command history?
run.historyClear.body: This empties the list of recent commands for {{name}}. Nothing on the computer changes.
run.terminalLife: It closes a minute after its window does.
run.noStartExpired: It has expired, so nothing can start it again.
run.secretHint: Commands that look like they contain a secret are not kept in history.
run.confirm.title: Run this command?
run.confirm.body: This command can delete data on {{name}}. It cannot be undone.
run.unknown.title: The command may have run
run.unknown.body: We did not get an answer. Check the output before running it again.
run.folder.refused.denied: Commands on {{name}} can't open this folder.
run.folder.refused.failed: This folder couldn't be opened on {{name}}. Try another folder.
run.folder.invalid.up: Write the folder from / without .. in it.
run.folder.invalid.long: That folder path is too long.
prog.title: Programs
prog.notRunning: {{name}} is not running, so its programs are stopped.
prog.col.name: Name
prog.noServer.body: This computer's server is not known yet, so its programs cannot be listed.
prog.emptyBody: Programs you install show up here.
prog.ask.body: This changes a program of the system. Continue?
ports.emptyBody: When a program opens a port it shows up here.
ports.notRunning: {{name}} is not running, so no ports are open.
ports.title: Ports
ports.help: Every port a program listens on; only web ports get an address on the internet.
ports.notRunningBody: Start it to see the ports its programs open.
ports.glance.title: At a glance
ports.glance.who.tip: The access rule of {{name}} decides who can open its web addresses and aliases, the same for every port. Ports that are not web have no address.
alias.title: Aliases
alias.col.name: Alias
alias.help: Short addresses that point to a web port, under the same access rule as the computer.
alias.emptyBody: Create one for any web port. Nothing needs to be running on it yet.
aliasd.title: Alias for port {{port}}
aliasd.kit: Hoody uses port {{port}}, so it can't have an alias.
aliasd.portRule: Type a port number from 1 to 65535.
aliasd.needPort: Enter the port this alias is for.
aliasd.needName: Enter a name for the alias.
aliasd.lede: An alias is a short, memorable address for a port.
aliasd.ledeAny: A short address for any port. Nothing needs to be running on it yet.
aliasd.name: Alias
aliasd.rule: 3 to 61 lowercase letters, numbers and dashes, not starting or ending with a dash.
aliasd.reserved: That name is kept for the platform. Pick another one.
aliasd.guess: The random ending keeps the address from being guessed. A short name of your own can be found by anyone who tries it.
aliasd.current: Now the port opens at its computer's own address.
aliasd.reminder: It follows this computer's access rule.
aliasd.guessWhy: Why does the suggested name end in random letters?
domaind.title: Use your own domain for {{name}}
domaind.lede: Open this alias at an address on a domain you own, such as app.example.com.
domaind.step: Where you manage your DNS, add a CNAME record that points to
domaind.copyTarget: Copy the address the record points to
domaind.route: One CNAME record sends your domain to this alias.
domaind.proxyOff: Turn off any proxy or CNAME flattening for this record
domaind.open: Wait for DNS, then open your address
domaind.blind: The Hub cannot see your DNS, so it cannot check this record for you.
domaind.name: Name
domaind.nameValue: The address you want, such as app (for app.example.com)
domaind.subdomain: Use a name under your domain, such as app.example.com. Most DNS companies don't allow this kind of record on the bare domain (example.com).
domaind.dnsOnly: A proxy is often shown as an orange cloud. With either one left on, your domain can't find the alias.
domaind.https: HTTPS is set up for you on the first visit, which can take a little while. If that first visit fails, wait a minute and open it again.
domaind.access: The computer's access rules still apply at your domain, just as at the alias.
domaind.wait: DNS changes take from a few minutes to a few hours to reach everyone.
domaind.undo: To stop, delete the record. If you also remove the alias, delete the record first: an alias name that is free again can be taken by someone else, and a record left behind would send your domain to them.
domaind.noHost: This alias has no address yet. Try again in a moment.
aliasr.title: Remove {{name}}?
aliasr.body: The alias stops working. The port stays open.
aliasr.cname: If a domain of yours points at this alias, delete that DNS record first: an alias name that is free again can be taken by someone else, and a record left behind would send your domain to them.
rename.title: Rename {{name}}
rename.label: New name
delete.title: Delete {{name}}
delete.body: This permanently deletes the computer and everything on it.
delete.c1: All files and programs are removed
realmsd.title: Realms of {{name}}
realmsd.lede: A realm is a separate space with its own computers, keys and settings. Pick it from the realm menu at the top. Tick every realm this computer should appear in. It can be in several.
realmsd.note: Keys and shared access limited to one realm see only the computers in it.
realmsd.now: Shown in the top bar now
importd.title: Add one of your computers to this realm
importd.lede: Pick a computer, then its realms: this one is already ticked, and it stays in any other realm you leave ticked.
importd.none: No computer in this list can be added to this realm.
importd.more: Only your first 100 computers are listed here.
projpick.owed: Pick a project for the new computer.
copyd.projectOutside: This computer's project is not in this realm. Pick a project here for the copy.
copyd.realmRefused: This realm did not allow the copy. The answer does not say which rule: the project, the source computer or the server picked may not be in this realm, or this login may not be allowed to do this here. Check the project, the computer's realms and the server, then try again.
copyd.noProject: This realm has no project yet, so a copy cannot be made here. Make a project in this realm first.
copyd.newProjectAskBody: The name you typed here is not kept. Copy {{name}} opens again after the new project.
copyd.title: Copy {{name}}
copyd.note: The copy starts with the same files.
field.name: Name

create.error.name: Use 3 to 100 letters, numbers, dashes or underscores.
create.error.nameReserved: The name rand is reserved. Type another name, or use Suggest another name.
create.error.noProject: This realm has no project yet, so a computer cannot be made here. Make a project in this realm, or pick All realms in the realm menu.
create.error.noProjectAny: You have no project yet, so a computer cannot be made. Make a project first.
create.error.projectGone: The project you picked is no longer listed here. Pick a project.
create.error.noProjectPinned: This realm has no project yet, so a computer cannot be made here. Make a project in this realm first.
create.newProjectAskTitle: Leave this form for New project?
create.newProjectOpen: Make the new project or cancel it first.
create.projectsLoading: Reading your projects. You can get the computer once they are in.
create.projectsFail: Could not load your projects, so nothing can be sent yet.
create.error.ssh_private: That looks like a private key. Paste the public key instead.
create.error.ssh_notkey: That is not a public SSH key.
create.error.color: Use a hex colour such as #4ECDC4.
create.error.kvmFree: Virtual machines need a paid server.
create.error.envKeyShape: A variable name has letters, numbers and underscores only.
create.error.envKeyLong: A variable name is too long.
create.error.envKeyReserved: Names starting with HOODY_ are reserved.
create.error.envKeyForbidden: That variable name is not allowed.
create.error.envValueNul: A value cannot contain a null character.
create.error.envValueUnicode: A value has an invalid character.
create.error.envTooBig: The variables are too large together.
create.title: Get a computer
create.lede: Everything is filled in for you. Change what you like, then get it.
create.ledeMissing: Something is missing. The box below says what.
create.ledeCopy: Pick one of your computers. The copy starts with the same files.
create.sum.label: You get
create.sum.stays: It stays stopped until you start it.
create.sum.sizeUnknown: Known once a server is picked
create.sum.serversUnread: Your servers could not be read.
create.sum.projectsUnread: Your projects could not be read.
create.sum.noProject: there is no project to put it in.
create.sum.projectGone: the project you picked is gone.
create.sum.fixRent: Get a new server from the Server list.
create.sum.fixFull: Delete a computer to make room.
create.sum.copyAny: A copy of one of your computers.
create.projectHelp: Groups computers. Its people and access rules apply to this one too.
create.moreWhat: Colour, software, SSH key, a note and variables. All optional.
create.nameHelp: Suggested for you. Keep it or type your own.
create.serverHelp: Computers on a server share its cores, memory and disk.
create.serverFull: Full. A paid plan has room for more computers.
create.sshHelp: Paste a public key to connect from your own SSH client.
create.sshOptional: Optional: Hoody Terminal opens in your browser without a key.
create.commentHelp: Optional. You, and any agent with access to your account, can read it through the API.
create.colorHelp: Marks it in lists. Picked at random.
create.fromCopy: A copy of one of yours
create.fromCopyHelp: Same files as the computer you pick.
create.copyNewProjectAskBody: What you typed in Get a computer is not kept. Get a computer opens again after the new project, still copying {{name}}.
create.realmsHelp: Each realm you add lists this computer too.
create.realmsWhy: What does adding a realm do?
create.realmHost: Always added: you're getting this computer inside this realm.
create.aiHelp: Programs on it can call Hoody AI, free model included, with no key. You can turn it off later.
create.autostartHelp: Start the computer as soon as it is ready.
create.devKitHelp: Node.js, Bun, Rust, Go, TypeScript and linters, installed when made.
create.hoodyKitHelp: Terminal, files, desktop, browser, editor and the Hoody agent. Only when made: it can't be added later.
create.kitOffTitle: Make this computer without the Hoody Kit?
create.kitOffBody: Without it the computer has no terminal, files, desktop, browser, code editor or Hoody agent in the Hub. Only SSH and its web addresses (http-/https-) work, and those answer only when something you run listens on the port. The kit can't be added later.
create.kvmHelp: Gives the computer /dev/kvm, so you can run VMs inside it. Only on servers allowed to run VMs: rented bare-metal servers.
create.envHelp: Values are kept secret and masked as you type.
srv.title: Servers
srv.col.name: Server
srv.capFull: Full: no room for another computer.
ov.expiredBand: {{name}} expired on {{date}}: its server ended or was reinstalled. Nothing can start it again.
ov.expiredBandNoDate: {{name}} has expired: its server ended or was reinstalled. Nothing can start it again.
ov.sharedCompute: Shared with the other free computers
ov.failed.CREATE_NOT_STARTED: The server could not take the new computer, so nothing was made on it. Delete this one and get a new computer.
ov.failed.CREATE_FAILED: Making this computer failed on its server. Delete this one and get a new computer.
ov.failed.COPY_FAILED: Copying into this computer failed on its server. Delete this one and make the copy again.
ov.kind.metal: A whole machine of your own
feat.title: Features
feat.about: What this computer has, on or off. Some can be changed here.
feat.madeWith: Chosen when the computer was made; it can't be changed after.
feat.hoody_kit.help: Terminal, files, desktop, browser, editor and the Hoody agent.
feat.dev_kit.help: Node.js, Bun, Rust, Go, TypeScript and linters.
feat.ai.help: Programs on it can call Hoody AI, free model included, with no key.
feat.ramdisk.help: Fast storage in memory at /ramdisk. A restart of its server empties it.
feat.autostart.help: Starts with its server: the computer starts by itself whenever its server starts.
feat.kvm.help: Lets this computer run its own virtual machines. It changes only while it is stopped.
feat.kvm.help.on: This computer can run its own virtual machines. It changes only while it is stopped.
feat.kvm.notAllowed: This server does not allow VMs, so KVM cannot be turned on.
feat.kvm.wait: It can change once the computer is stopped or running.
feat.kvm.kindUnknown: Could not check what kind of server this computer is on.
feat.kvm.help.shared: Only on a bare-metal server. This computer runs on shared hardware.
feat.kvm.why.title: KVM needs a bare-metal server
feat.kvm.why.body: KVM lets a computer run its own virtual machines. On shared hardware the /dev/kvm device cannot be shared safely, so KVM needs a bare-metal server.
feat.why.expired: This computer has expired, so this cannot change.
feat.why.notOwner: Only the owner of its project can change this.
feat.why.noRight: This access key may not change computers.
feat.why.framed: Open the Hub in its own tab to change this.
feat.held.on: Turning on {{what}} for {{name}} may have gone through. It is not confirmed yet.
feat.held.off: Turning off {{what}} for {{name}} may have gone through. It is not confirmed yet.
feat.ask.ramdiskOff.title: Turn off the RAM disk for {{name}}?
feat.ask.ramdiskOff.body: /ramdisk is taken away from the computer. Files kept there may be lost.
on.title: On {{name}}
on.programs.notRunning: Start the computer to see them run
srv.emptyBody: Servers you can use show up here.
zero.empty.title: No computers here yet
zero.empty.body: Get your first computer to begin.
zero.empty.bodyNoCreate: This login can't get computers. Open Computers with a login that can, such as the account owner's.
zero.empty.bodyElsewhere: Get a computer here, or add one you already have. All your computers are listed when you pick All realms in the realm menu.
zero.unknown.title: We couldn't check whether a computer is being set up
zero.unknown.oldBody: This browser still keeps a computer request from an earlier visit, and we can't tell whether it went through. If you know it didn't, stop tracking it to create a computer.
zero.provisioning.title: Your first computer is being prepared
zero.provisioning.heldBody: A computer you asked for may have been made. Check whether it went through.
zero.provisioning.heldNoCreate: A computer you asked for may have been made. This login can't check it: open Computers with a login that can get computers, such as the account owner's, and choose Check on it.

zero.capacity.title: No room right now

zero.mailbox.title: Check your email
zero.mailbox.body: We sent you a message to finish setting up.
zero.expired.title: Your access has ended
zero.expired.body: Renew your subscription to get a computer.
zero.reinstalled.title: Your server was reinstalled
zero.reinstalled.body: The computers on it are gone. Delete them in Projects, then create a new computer.

create.refused.SERVER_COMPUTER_LIMIT: That server has no room left. Pick another server.

pp.fact.rules.level: Only the owner and Full control see these
pp.title: Permissions of {{name}}
pp.cx.title: Computers in {{name}} (all realms)
pp.cx.lede: Each computer adds its own rules, if it has any, to the project's. Expired and deleting computers are listed too.
pp.cx.unknownNote: "Not known": the Hub can't yet tell whether this computer keeps an answer of its own for everyone not in a group. Open its access to see its rules.
pp.cx.unknownNoteMember: "Not known": the Hub can't yet tell whether this computer keeps an answer of its own for everyone not in a group.
pp.cx.more: Showing the first {{count}}. The counts above cover only these.
pp.cx.reinstalledOf: {{name}}: the server it ran on was reinstalled, and its files are gone. Delete it to free its name.
pp.cx.empty: No computers in this project yet.
pp.cx.cantRead.key: An access key can't list the project's computers.
pp.ov.lede: This project passes two things to every computer in it, now and later, in every realm: its people and its access rules.
pp.ov.realms.value: Not shared with realms. Each computer keeps its own.
pp.cx.col.name: Computer
pp.cx.factsOf: Counted over the computers shown below.
pp.busy: Wait for the change being sent to finish.
pp.add.open: The form to add a person is open below.
pp.ov.rules.none: No project rules. Each computer's own rules decide; a computer with none is open to anyone with its address.
pp.ov.rules.noCounts: Computers with rules of their own keep their own answer for everyone not in a group and inherit the project's groups and rules.
pp.ov.explainPromise: Explain sends the Agent these rules and computers, never passwords or keys. This drawer wins if they disagree.
pp.ov.people.none: No other accounts are members of this project.
pp.ov.people.uncounted: The Hub couldn't tell who else is on this project. People shows what it read.
pp.rules.title: Who can open the programs of {{name}}'s computers
pp.rules.ledeFull: For a computer without rules of its own, this decides who gets in.
pp.rules.ledeAdded: For a computer with rules of its own, these groups are added to its rules.
pp.rules.none: No project rules. Each computer decides with its own rules.
pp.rules.hooksIgnored: Hooks on a project are not used. Only a computer's own hooks run.
pp.rules.cantRead.key: An access key can't read project rules: they hold passwords and keys that open every computer in the project.
pp.rules.cantRead.level: Only the owner and people with Full control can see these rules.
pp.rules.error: Couldn't read the project's access rules.
pp.rules.facts: Groups and what they may open
pp.rules.c.noneHelp: Each computer decides with its own rules. Computers without rules of their own become open to anyone with their address; the others lose the groups and rules they inherited.
pp.rules.c.myIpHelp: Computers without rules of their own open only from the address you use now. Computers with rules of their own inherit this group.
pp.rules.c.ipsHelp: Computers without rules of their own open only from the addresses you list. Computers with rules of their own inherit these groups.
pp.rules.c.privateHelp: Computers without rules of their own can't be opened by address. Computers with rules of their own lose the groups and rules they inherited from the project.
pp.rules.changed: These rules changed since they were shown. What's shown now is what applies: check it, then press Save… again.
pp.rules.ipChanged: The address you use now changed since it was shown. What's shown now is your current address: check it, then press Save… again.
pp.rules.listFailed: Couldn't list this project's computers, so the Hub can't say what the change does to them. Nothing was changed.

faq.whatYouGet.q: What does a new computer come with?
faq.whatYouGet.a: New computers run Debian 13 for now. You can still run your own containers inside, with Docker or Podman for example. The Hoody Kit gives you the terminal, files, desktop, browser, code editor and the Hoody agent, opened from the Hub. It can only be added when the computer is made, not later. Programs on the computer can also call Hoody AI, including the free model, with no key to set up. You can turn that off later.
faq.realmsAndProjects.a: A realm is a separate space with its own computers, keys and settings. Pick it from the realm menu at the top. A computer can be in several realms: each realm you add lists it too, and it can be managed from that realm. You can change this later in Realms. A project groups computers, and its colour marks it in lists. A project passes two things to every computer in it, now and later, in every realm: its people and its access rules.
faq.whoCanOpen.q: Who can open my computer's programs?
faq.whoCanOpen.a: This covers the computer's programs opened through their web addresses: terminal, files, display and the others. You choose one of five. Anyone with the address: no sign-in; anyone with a program's address can open it. Only my IP: only connections from the address you are using now. Only these IPs: the addresses you list. Only people or keys I pick: each person signs in with a name and password, or opens a link that carries a key. Private: nobody, you included. The project has access rules too, so a computer's rules alone may not tell who gets in. Change it in the computer's Permissions tab.
faq.firewall.q: How does the firewall work, and what does No internet block?
faq.firewall.a: The firewall covers all traffic into and out of the computer. Block and Refuse rules apply before allow rules whatever their order, and unmatched traffic is allowed, so allow rules alone restrict nothing. Hoody applies it outside the computer: programs and root inside can't change it directly, but a key allowed to manage firewalls, including the agent's key, can. Blocking internet access stops new outbound connections (TCP, UDP and IPv4 ping) and leaves inbound traffic alone, so programs stay reachable through their URLs. To limit one program instead, use its Sandbox under Programs.
faq.proxyAndExit.q: How do I use a computer as a proxy, and what is an exit?
faq.proxyAndExit.a: Every computer is also a proxy: put its address in any browser, app or script to send traffic out through it, an HTTP proxy over an encrypted connection. Traffic leaves from its own IP address and reaches public IPv4 addresses only, unless you set another exit, which then decides which sites work. To check, open https://ip.hoody.com through it. To send all its traffic through a VPN such as Mullvad, not just the proxy's (exits still work), add an SSH key first, then run the provider's WireGuard file with wg-quick, not its app, whose kill switch cuts the computer's addresses and web terminal.
faq.ownDomain.q: How do I use my own domain for a web address?
faq.ownDomain.a: First make an alias, a short, memorable address for a port. Once it exists, use Use your own domain in the Aliases list. At your DNS company add the record shown, with a name under your domain, such as app.example.com. Most DNS companies don't allow this kind of record on the bare domain. If your DNS company offers a proxy or CNAME flattening, turn it off for this record. HTTPS is set up for you the first time someone opens the address. The computer's access rules still apply at your domain.
faq.sshAndTerminal.q: How do I get a shell on my computer?
faq.sshAndTerminal.a: There are three ways: the terminal in your browser, which needs the computer running and no key; direct SSH from your own terminal with your public key; or the Hoody command line, after you install it and sign in. A key can be on one computer only. A temporary terminal closes about a minute after you close its window (later while something in it is still printing), and reloading it opens a new one. Programs you started in the background keep running. For a terminal that stays, put one on the Board.
faq.snapshotsAndBackups.q: What is the difference between a snapshot and a zip backup?
faq.snapshotsAndBackups.a: A snapshot saves the whole computer as it is now, kept by Hoody, and you can start a new computer from any of them. A zip backup downloads chosen folders of the computer to your device as .zip files, one per folder; the download goes straight from the computer to your browser. Restoring a snapshot puts the computer back to how it was when the snapshot was taken, and files and settings changed since then are lost.
